$comment: THE GUARD REGISTRY — every enforcement promise this platform makes.
`scripts/guards.test.mjs` reads this file. Three rules make it more than a
1. A `live` guard must name an implementation AND a literal string that
implementation contains. Rename or delete the check and the registry
fails — so a guard cannot quietly stop existing.
2. A `live` guard must actually RUN: an .mjs guard is named by the root
`gate` or `one:gate` script, a .ts guard sits where the test runner
finds it. A check nobody invokes is the same as no check.
3. An `owed` guard names a stage, and ⚠️ a SHIPPED stage may owe
nothing. This is the DEFER mechanism applied to enforcement: flipping a
stage to shipped is what forces every guard it promised to be built,
re-targeted with a reason, or dropped on purpose.
And the tables in PLAN.md §6 and UI.md §10 are GENERATED from this file, so
prose cannot promise a guard that has no entry here — which is the failure
this registry exists for. Documentation claiming enforcement nobody built is
worse than no documentation, because it is expensive to disprove.

guards.fails: a governed document with no `kind` in its front matter, or a contract with no `verified:` date
a deferral with no id, a duplicate id, no description, an unknown stage — or a stage that is SHIPPED
a generated block whose command now produces different output — a hand-edited inventory
a document no other document links to
guards.proves: is not linked from any other document

guards.fails: a guard claimed in prose with no registry entry, a live guard whose check has been renamed or deleted, a live guard nothing invokes, or a shipped stage still owing one
a module importing one at its own layer or above
a day-zero declaration from MANIFEST.md §9 with no type expressing it, or one expressed as optional
a product noun in kernel code — an identifier, a type or a string literal
an escape hatch on a manifest type — a passthrough, a raw blob, an unchecked extension point
an exported symbol no proof or test exercises
an `any` with no stated reason beside it
a module applied with no surface mounted to reach it
any runtime binding touched outside its owner — a query that will hit the wrong continent the day a second region exists
a KV write outside the allow-listed key space — the one store that cannot be regionalised may never hold anything personal
a column on the global tenant directory outside the routing-data allow-list
a route, tool or webhook that did not come from `operation()`
an AI tool reachable where the equivalent route is not
a failure body that is not a `Problem`, a code with no copy, or a `catch` that re-throws or serialises a provider's error
a table carrying a scope column and declaring none
a module ordered where its dependency has not run
a Durable Object class that cannot seal, export and import its state
a bounded sweep that does not log what it dropped
a sold entitlement no gate names
a sold capability the UI hides and no route withholds
a deploy removing a plan, permission or entitlement somebody holds
an app's own suite crossing its duration cap — the fixture problem gets solved rather than tolerated
a help article over its length limit, naming a surface the manifest does not declare, or using developer vocabulary
a release note reading like a commit message — a file path, a type name, a PR number, an internal id
a screenshot id the suite does not produce
any brand-slot combination in range producing ink below its floor, at either theme, on any ground
a colour value anywhere outside the token layer
a duration, easing curve, `@keyframes` or transition property outside the choreographer
a registered component with a state it does not declare and photograph
a data container whose pending and empty states resolve to the same render
a `disabled` prop with no accompanying explanation
an entitlement or permission rendered as `disabled` rather than `locked`
an app defining a shell, dialog, toast, empty state or form primitive; a raw `<button>` or `<input>`
an interaction reachable only by hover
a pane-capable surface sized by viewport breakpoints rather than by its container
a second destination surface at any width
an interactive element whose hit area resolves below the floor
a second surface declared live, or a live surface remounted between presentations
a layout that depends on an animation having run
